s: an entire street devoted to Tokyo's own liquid-style okonomiyaki
w: A shitamachi shopping street lined almost entirely with monjayaki restaurants -- Tokyo's own runnier, messier cousin of okonomiyaki, cooked and scraped at the table with a tiny metal spatula. More than 70 shops along Nishinaka-dori keep the ritual alive on an island reclaimed from Tokyo Bay, a genuine old-downtown specialty rather than a tourist invention.
_facts: Runs along Nishinaka-dori on Tsukishima, an island in Chuo Ward reclaimed from Tokyo Bay
Home to more than 70 monjayaki restaurants along a single street
Monjayaki is a liquid-batter, griddle-cooked dish distinct from the thicker okonomiyaki
A short walk from Tsukishima Station on the Oedo and Yurakucho lines

s: Tokyo's street-food market that outlived the wholesale move to Toyosu
w: When the Tsukiji wholesale fish market relocated to Toyosu in 2018, the surrounding outer market of stalls and small restaurants stayed put -- and kept its energy. Narrow covered lanes still sell fresh seafood, knives, tamagoyaki and quick counter meals, busy with locals and early risers as much as visitors chasing the market's old name.
_facts: Located around Tsukiji, Chuo Ward, Tokyo, near Tsukiji Station
The inner wholesale fish market relocated to Toyosu in October 2018; the outer market of shops and eateries remained at Tsukiji
Known for fresh seafood stalls, kitchenware shops and small eat-in counters
